parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe the independent groups experimental design and outline how it was used in the
study by Piliavin et al.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Design an alternative way to investigate bystander behaviour which uses a laboratory
experiment and describe how it could be conducted.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Evaluate this alternative way of studying bystander behaviour in methodological and ethical
terms.

text: Piliavin et al. (subway Samaritans) conducted a field study to investigate bystander behaviour.
An alternative way to collect data would be to conduct a laboratory experiment.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What is meant by the ‘nature-nurture debate’?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe how the results of the Billington et al. study support either the nature or the nurture
side of the debate.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Discuss the strengths and weaknesses of the individual differences approach using the study
by Billington et al. as an example.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
Compare the individual differences approach with one other approach in psychology using
the Billington et al. study and any other study as examples. 
Section B (20 marks)
Answer one question from this section.

text: Billington et al. (empathising and systemising) conducted a self report study to investigate cognitive
style and subject choice in university students.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the ‘developmental approach’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Langlois et al. (infant facial preference)
Nelson (children’s morals)
Freud (little Hans)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how the data were collected in each of these studies.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What advantages may psychologists have when they investigate the developmental
approach?

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline what is meant by the term ‘validity’ in psychology. 
Using the studies from the list below, answer the questions which follow:
Haney, Banks and Zimbardo (prison simulation)
Veale and Riley (mirror gazing)
Loftus and Pickrell (false memories)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe how each of these studies is valid.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
What problems may psychologists have when they try to make their studies valid?
